text: dsh-diff-review 是面向 DSH Web 的变更审阅插件，会在右侧侧栏提供独立审阅面板，并从 Host 获取每轮文件差异。用户可以浏览最近轮次和文件、查看行级差异、逐文件确认或回退，也能添加审阅备注并发送到下一轮对话。它还支持整轮操作和恢复回退。适合希望在 DSH 中逐项检查 agent 修改的用户；需要带 Web UI 的 DSH profile。

dsh-diff-review adds a change review pane to the DSH Web right sidebar. It loads turn diffs from the Host so users can browse recent turns and files, inspect line changes, confirm files, leave notes for the next turn, and revert or restore file changes. Requires a DSH profile with the Web UI.
想在 DSH Web 里逐个文件检查 agent 这一轮改了什么。
能不能逐个确认变更，并把某个文件恢复到修改前？
I want to leave file-specific review notes and carry them into my next DSH turn.
dsh-diff-review 的功能「逐文件查看每轮差异」：侧栏展示最近的会话轮次和变更文件，可打开文件查看差异块并在差异间导航。
dsh-diff-review 的功能「确认、备注与回退变更」：用户可记录逐文件确认、添加或编辑审阅备注，也可回退单个文件或整轮并恢复回退；备注可发送到 composer。

dsh-diff-review README · dsh-diff-review：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A review pane for DSH: read a turn's diffs one file at a time, confirm each file separately, revert a file (or the whole turn) back to how it was before, and leave review notes for the next turn.

DSH already ships a read-only change viewer. This plugin is the other half — the one that writes.

dsh-diff-review README · What it does：| Action | Scope | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Confirm | one file / whole turn | no — records a decision only |
| Revert | one file / whole turn | yes — writes the file back |
| Undo revert | one file / whole turn | yes — writes the change forward again |
| Edit (note) | one file | no — becomes text in the composer |

dsh-diff-review README · What it does：Everything else is reading: the turn list, the file list, per-file hunks with word-level highlighting, and the decision state. A turn that changed nothing and a turn still running are shown as different things, so the pane never sits on "still running" forever.

Reverting a turn is streamed: the Host plans every file first (read-only), then writes them one by one and reports progress per file. A file that cannot be planned is reported and skipped instead of aborting the batch.

dsh-diff-review README · Install：The plugin is a normal DSH bundle. It is not on npm yet, so install it from a checkout.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pastchais/dsh-diff-review.git
cd dsh-diff-review
```

Then, from the DSH Web UI, open **Plugins → install a bundle** and point it at the checkout:

```
link:<absolute path to the checkout>
```

Or from an agent session with `plugin_manager` enabled:

```
plugin_manager(action: "install_bundle", target: "link:<absolute path to the checkout>")
```

dsh-diff-review README · Install：The install enables the bundle by default. With HMR configured in the profile, the browser half reloads on `ctrl+r`; without it, restart DSH.

If you would rather run it from source without installing, point HMR at the checkout instead — this is what the development setup uses:

```yaml

dsh-diff-review README · <dshHome>/cordis.hmr.patch.yml：- id: hmr
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-hmr'
  config:
    base: file:///<absolute path to the checkout>
    root: ['.']
    debounce: 100
```

Requirements: a DSH profile with the Web UI. The pane registers into the right Sidebar, so `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right` must be present (it is, in every shipped Web profile). Nothing else is mandatory — see [Limitations](#limitations) for what degrades when a service is missing.

dsh-diff-review README · Use it：**Open the pane.** Each finished turn with recorded changes ends with an "Review in sidebar" button; the pane also appears as a **Change review** tab in the right Sidebar.

**Pick a turn.** The header has a turn picker offering the newest recorded turns. It remembers the *turn number*, not a position, so new turns arriving at the top do not change what you are looking at.

dsh-diff-review README · Use it：**Walk the files.** `↑` / `↓` move through the file list, `Enter` confirms the selected file. Each row shows its own `+added −deleted` count, a state dot, and a **new** badge for files the turn created.

**Walk the changes.** `F7` jumps to the next change inside the open file, `Shift+F7` to the previous one. The header shows `1 / N` blocks.

**Act on a file.** The three header buttons work on the file you are looking at:

dsh-diff-review README · Use it：- **Confirm** records "I have read this". Press again to take the record back.
- **Revert** writes the file back to its pre-turn content, then turns into **Undo revert**.
- **Edit** opens a note box. Saved notes are listed under the diff and can be edited (✎) or dropped (×).

dsh-diff-review README · Use it：**Finish the turn.** The footer shows `confirmed X / N`, **Confirm all**, **Revert turn**, and — once notes exist — **Send to composer**, which folds every note into one Markdown block and appends it to whatever you already typed, without overwriting it.

dsh-diff-review README · How it avoids clobbering your work：Reverting is the only destructive action, and it is guarded three ways.

**Round-trip check.** A revert is computed as "apply the turn's patch backwards". Before writing, the result is pushed forward again and compared byte for byte with what is on disk:

```
before = reverseApply(hunks, current)
forwardApply(hunks, before) === current     // must hold, or nothing is written
```
section: How it avoids clobbering your work

text:
dsh-diff-review README · How it avoids clobbering your work：This one check covers CRLF, a missing trailing newline, and coarse patches that degraded to "replace the whole file" — the three cases where a naive reverse-apply silently corrupts a file.

**Optimistic locking.** The write goes through the filesystem with `replaceIfVersion` using the version observed a moment earlier, or `createIfAbsent` for a file the turn deleted. If anything touched the file in between, the write is refused rather than retried.
section: How it avoids clobbering your work

text:
dsh-diff-review README · How it avoids clobbering your work：**Per-file reporting.** A batch is planned completely before any byte is written, so a refused file leaves the rest untouched. Failures come back as codes (`STALE`, `COARSE`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `MISSING`) that the browser localizes; the Host never sends user-facing prose.

Reverting a file the turn *created* cannot delete it — the filesystem seam has no delete — so it is **emptied** and the UI says so, both in the list ("new") and in the result message.

text:
dsh-diff-review README · Files it creates：| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| `<dshHome>/storages/diff_review.json` | decisions and review notes, durable across restarts |
| the reviewed files themselves | only when you revert or undo a revert |

dsh-diff-review README · Files it creates：Turn snapshots and diffs are **not** stored by this plugin. They come from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace-changes`, which keeps them in memory for the life of the Host process; after a restart the pane offers only the turns that Host can still serve. Decisions and notes survive, because they are in the storage unit above.

dsh-diff-review README · Appearance: font, size, colour：The plugin hard-codes **no colour and no font size**. Everything resolves against the running theme and against DSH's own appearance settings, so "Settings → Appearance" changes it for free and switching light/dark needs no plugin change.

dsh-diff-review README · Appearance: font, size, colour：- **Fonts** follow `--dsw-font-family` (prose) and `--ds-font-family-code` (diffs, line numbers).
- **Sizes** follow `--dsh-content-font-delta` / `--dsh-code-font-delta`, the deltas DSH puts on `body` when you change the text or code size.
- **Colours** are `var(--dsw-alias-*)` tokens only, including `--dsw-alias-file-diff-*` for the diff bands.

Three ways to change it, lightest first:

dsh-diff-review README · Appearance: font, size, colour：1. Install a theme plugin, or override `--dsw-alias-*` in your profile. This pane follows.
2. Add a CSS override — every rule is scoped under `.dr-root`:

```css
   .dr-root .dr-line[data-k=add] { background: #e8f5e9; }
   ```

3. Edit the `const CSS` array in `lib/client.js`; with HMR a `ctrl+r` is enough.

Word-level highlighting uses `color-mix()` over the theme's marker colours, because the theme has no per-word token. The percentage is one number if you want it louder or quieter.

dsh-diff-review README · Appearance: font, size, colour：See [docs/appearance.md](docs/appearance.md) for the full table of tokens, the current size scale, and a checklist for verifying that nothing is hard-coded.

dsh-diff-review README · Development：```
lib/index.js            Host half: 12 authenticated routes, decision + note store, revert
lib/patch.js            pure patch math: reverseApply / forwardApply / round-trips
lib/client.js           browser half: tab, turn picker, diff view, notes, composer hand-off
test/patch.mjs          patch math against real structuredPatch output (14 cases)

```bash
npm test          # all three suites, no dependencies to install
```

dsh-diff-review README · Development：The tests are contract tests: they drive the plugin's own exports against hand-written doubles for the Host services, so they run in plain Node with no build step and no DSH running. The patch math is tested separately against real `structuredPatch` output, because that is the part that can corrupt a file.

dsh-diff-review README · Development：The Host half imports nothing but `./patch.js` — a plugin installed into a profile cannot resolve `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages, so the storage domain spec and its record schemas are declared by hand.

dsh-diff-review README · Design notes：[`docs/revert-plan.md`](docs/revert-plan.md) is the design note behind the revert and note features, including the parts that changed while building it and the mistakes worth not repeating:

dsh-diff-review README · Design notes：- `AbortSignal.any` rejects an `undefined` entry, so a recorder read without a signal throws.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-sandbox` falls back to the *deployment* policy when none is passed, which is narrower than the Session's — a revert must pass `sandboxPolicy.resolve({ session })` or it is denied.
- The storage unit is in `single` layout, where `compatibleVersions` does not apply: adding a table is safe, bumping the version orphans every existing record.
- `ctx.fs` has no delete, which is why a created file is emptied rather than removed.

dsh-diff-review README · Limitations：- **In-memory turn records.** The Host keeps snapshots in memory; after a restart, older turns are gone from the picker rather than shown as broken.
- **One layout.** Unified diffs only, with a fixed 3 lines of context, as recorded by the Host.
- **No deletes.** Reverting a created file empties it; removing the file is yours to do.
- **Degrades, never crashes.** Without `storageDomain` the pane reads but cannot record (503). Without `fs` it reads and records but cannot revert. Without `sessions` the turn picker and latest-turn detection stop. Without `conversation` the "send to composer" button stops. The diff itself needs `workspaceChanges`; without it the pane shows its empty state.
